newsitem.title: USA: NCAA-TOP-RANKED KANSAS WINS OPENER AS MARCH MADNESS BEGINS.
newsitem.headline: NCAA-TOP-RANKED KANSAS WINS OPENER AS MARCH MADNESS BEGINS.

text.p: Top-ranked Kansas took the first step on the road to the Final Four Thursday with a convincing victory on the opening day of the 1997 NCAA men's college basketball tournament.
Scot Pollard had 12 points, 19 rebounds and five blocked shots to lead top-seeded Kansas to a 78-64 victory over 16th-seeded Jackson State in the Southeast Region opener.
Cincinnati and California also posted early wins in the 64-team tournament as "March Madness" got underway with play at four regional sites.
Paul Pierce added 19 points for Kansas, which broke open the game early in the second half after Jackson State had pulled within eight points at 51-43.
The Jayhawks (33-1) will next play the winner of the Purdue-Rhode Island game in the second round Saturday.
Trent Pulliam scored 22 points to lead Jackson State (14-16), which was making its first NCAA Tournament appearance after winning the Southwestern Athletic Conference Tournament.
Jackson State was one of only two schools with a losing record to earn a coveted berth into the tournament. Fairfield (11-18), which opens against North Carolina Thursday night, is the other.
At Auburn Hills, Danny Fortson scored 24 points and Darnell Burton added 18 as third-seeded Cincinnati soundly defeated 14th-seeded Butler 86-69 in the Midwest Region.
The Cincinnati Bearcats (26-7) will play the winner of the Iowa State-Illinois State game in the second round.
Burton drained three three-pointers, Fortson had eight points and Damon Flint dished out seven assists in the first half as as Cincinnati rolled to a 39-17 halftime lead and never looked back.
Kelsey Wilson and Jon Neuhouser scored 15 points apiece for Butler (23-10), which was in the NCAA Tournament for the first time since 1962.

At Winston-Salem, Tony Gonzalez hit a fadeaway jumper with 58 seconds remaining to snap a tie and added three free throws in the final 36 seconds to lead fifth-seeded California to a 55-52 victory over 12th-seeded Princeton in the East Region.
California (22-8) will play the winner of the Villanova-Long Island University game in the second round.
Gonzalez broke a 50-50 tie with a 12-foot jumper and added a free-throw for a three-point lead with 32 seconds left.
Princeton pulled within 53-52 on a layup by Brian Earl with 15.6 seconds remaining. But Gonzalez added two more free throws for the final winning margin.
Princeton had a chance to tie the game, but California's Alfred Grigsby blocked a three-point attempt by Gabe Lewullis with four seconds left, ending the Ivy League champion's 19-game winning streak.
